record.context_brief: How much dispersal-controlled sign symmetry forces stability
record.original_question: Fix an integer d. Let A be a P-matrix, and assume that the sign-symmetry inequalities A[α, β]A[β, α] ≥ 0 hold for every minor whose dispersal #α - #(α ∩ β) is at most d. What is the smallest value of d that guarantees stability of A, meaning that all eigenvalues of A have positive real part? Does this minimal stability-forcing value of d depend on the matrix order n?

evidence.quote: Given α, β ∈ hni with #α = #β, call the number #α − #(α ∩ β) the dispersal of the minor A[α, β].

2. Dispersal condition sufficient for stability. The counterexample given in [11] shows that it is not sufficient for stability of a P-matrix A that the inequalities (1) hold for all minors of dispersal less than or equal to d = 1. Carlson’s theorem [3] asserts that the value d = n is sufficient for stability (in other words, that sign￾symmetric matrices are stable). What minimal value of the parameter d would guarantee stability? In particular, does that value depend on n?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n\ge 2$ and let $A=(a_{ij})$ be an $n\times n$ real matrix. Recall that $A$ is called a P-matrix if every principal minor of $A$ is positive, and $A$ is called (positive) stable if every eigenvalue of $A$ has positive real part. For index sets $\alpha,\beta\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\}$ with $|\alpha|=|\beta|$, write $A[\alpha,\beta]$ for the minor with row index set $\alpha$ and column index set $\beta$, and define the dispersal of this minor to be $|\alpha|-|\alpha\cap\beta|$.

For a nonnegative integer $d$, say that $A$ satisfies the dispersal-$d$ sign symmetry condition if 
$$A[\alpha,\beta]\,A[\beta,\alpha]\;\ge\;0$$
for every pair $\alpha,\beta\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\}$ with $|\alpha|=|\beta|$ and dispersal $|\alpha|-|\alpha\cap\beta|\le d$.

It is known that the choice $d=n$ (full sign symmetry) is sufficient to force stability of every P-matrix of order $n$, while $d=1$ is not sufficient.

Determine the smallest integer $d=d(n)$ such that every $n\times n$ P-matrix satisfying the dispersal-$d$ sign symmetry condition is stable. In particular, decide whether this minimal value $d$ depends on the order $n$ of the matrix.
artifact.status_search_result: A survey on GKK and τ-matrices discusses this dispersal sufficient-for-stability question and presents it as an unresolved problem; counterexamples are known for $d=1$ and Carlson's theorem covers $d=n$, but the minimal sufficient $d$ and its dependence on $n$ do not appear to have been pinned down in subsequent literature.

status_evidence.title: Theorems and counterexamples on structured matrices
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses GKK τ-matrix conjectures, sign-symmetry/dispersal conditions, Carlson's theorem and counterexamples for small dispersal.
status_evidence.claim: The dispersal sufficient-for-stability question is discussed as still open in the literature; only the extreme cases d=1 (insufficient) and d=n (Carlson, sufficient) are established.

status_evidence.title: Not all GKK τ-matrices are stable
status_evidence.snippet: Provides counterexamples disproving the conjecture that all GKK τ-matrices are stable.
status_evidence.claim: Counterexamples show weak sign-symmetry alone (related to low dispersal) is insufficient to force stability.
